description: Parade day: Frog falls asleep counting socks one by one, so Robo leads skip counting by 2s (pairs of socks), 5s (hands) and 10s (bunches of balloons) while Frog leaps along a number line road, finds the patterns on a 20 chart, compares jump sizes and takes a parade quiz.

youtube.title: Skip Counting by 2s, 5s and 10s for Kids! Parade Song | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
It's parade day! Frog tries to count twenty socks one at a time and falls asleep, so Robo shows a faster way: skip counting. Count pairs of socks by 2s to 20, hands by 5s to 50 and bunches of balloons by 10s to 100, while Frog leaps along a number line painted on the road. Kids spot the patterns (2, 4, 6, 8, 0 again; fives end in 5 or 0; tens end in 0), catch Robo skipping a number and take a parade quiz.

For first graders (CCSS 1.NBT.A.1, 1.OA.C.5).

Try at home: with a grown-up, pair up socks from the laundry and count them by 2s. Trace your hand and count fingers by 5s. Small things like buttons and pasta are not for mouths; keep them away from babies, and hop on a flat, safe surface.

do.text: Parade day! The band needs twenty socks.
I'll count them. One... two... three...
Frog, wake up! There's a faster way.
Let's skip count! Skip counting is a fast way to count groups.
Socks come in pairs. A pair means two.
So we count the pairs by twos.
Ooh! Can we count by a MILLION?
Ha! Let's start with twos, Frog.
Twenty socks for the band! Thank you!
Now the road. Frog, jump two numbers each time.
Watch. He skips over one. Lands on two.
Say it loud: two, four, six, eight, ten!
Here are the numbers one to twenty.
Let's color every number we said.
Look at the ones digits. Two, four, six, eight, zero.
Then again! Two, four, six, eight, zero.
It's a pattern! Every other number!
Twelve, fourteen, sixteen... what comes next?
Count them: one, two, three, four, five.
Now the road counts by fives. Bigger jumps!
Wait. Did I count right? Five, ten, twenty?
Thank you! Fifteen comes before twenty.
Fives end in five or zero. Five, ten, fifteen, twenty!
Balloons! I tie them in bunches of ten.
One hundred balloons! That's ten tens!
My turn! Giant jumps, all the way to one hundred!
One hundred! My biggest jump ever!
Tens all end in zero. Ten, twenty, thirty!
Three friends race to ten. Frog jumps by twos.
Bunny jumps by fives. Bear jumps by tens. Go!
Five jumps of two. Two jumps of five. One jump of ten.
Quiz time! Two, four, six... what comes next?
Five, ten, fifteen... what comes next?
Ten, twenty, thirty, something, fifty. What's missing?
Six pairs of socks. Count by twos. How many socks?
Two, four, six, eight, ten, twelve! Twelve socks!
Last one. Counting by tens from zero. Do we land on thirty-five or seventy?
Seventy! Tens end in zero. No thirty-five.
Everyone, march and count by tens with the drum!
Skip counting is counting in equal jumps.
By twos, by fives, by tens, all the way to one hundred!
Skip, skip, don't stop! Count in jumps to the top!
